question: In bacterial meningitis, the CSF differential shows predominantly neutrophils (polymorphonuclear cells), whereas in viral (aseptic) meningitis, lymphocytes predominate.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. The CSF differential cell count is the key discriminator: neutrophil (PMN) predominance → bacterial; lymphocyte predominance → viral. Additional discriminators include very low CSF glucose (<40 mg/dL) and very high protein (>200 mg/dL) in bacterial meningitis vs. near-normal glucose in viral.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The neutrophil-versus-lymphocyte differential is the single most important cell-type discriminator in CSF analysis. Bacterial meningitis = PMN pleocytosis (typically >500 cells/μL, predominantly neutrophils). Viral meningitis = lymphocytic pleocytosis (usually <500 cells/μL). Note: early viral meningitis may show initial neutrophilia that shifts to lymphocytes within 24 hours.
